themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Boom or Blight?
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score 5.67), suggesting either rapid expansion of dining infrastructure or widespread enforcement complaints tied to the three active rezonings (Avenue U, Shell Road, Avenue Y) that may be altering streetscape use patterns.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike)
Three active ULURP rezonings in district pipeline suggest commercial/mixed-use intensification
reporting_angles: Are restaurant owners rapidly expanding outdoor seating ahead of zoning changes?
What code violations are driving complaints—spacing, hours, obstruction?

themes_detail.label: Street Obstructions Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped 197% to 29 complaints two weeks ago vs. 9.8 weekly average (z-score 6.63), indicating significant sidewalk or street blockages that may be linked to the concurrent dead/dying tree spike (418% increase) or construction activity from 592 DOB permits filed.
evidence: 29 obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.8 weekly average (197% increase, z-score 6.63)
Dead/dying tree complaints also spiked 418% (11 last week vs. 2.1 avg)—possible root cause
592 DOB alteration permits filed in last 90 days may be generating debris/sidewalk closures
reporting_angles: Are fallen or dying trees the primary cause of obstruction complaints?
Is construction activity from 592 permits creating chronic sidewalk blockages?

themes_detail.label: Dead Tree Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints surged 418% to 11 last week vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score 5.78), the second-highest statistical anomaly in the district, suggesting either disease outbreak, storm damage, or deferred maintenance in parks and streetscapes.
evidence: 11 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly baseline (418% increase, z-score 5.78)
Correlated with obstruction spike (may be blocking sidewalks/roads)
No recent news or CB discussion suggests issue may be under-reported or newly accelerating
reporting_angles: Are trees dying from disease, pest infestation, or weather stress?
What is Parks Dept. response time for removal in Sheepshead Bay?
Is this linked to broader citywide tree health issues?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Uptick in Waterfront District
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped 433% to 8 two weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score 4.91), suggesting either increased homelessness or visible encampments concentrated near transit/parks—worth investigating alongside concurrent obstruction and tree complaints that may indicate deteriorating public space conditions.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (433% increase, z-score 4.91)
Concurrent with obstruction and tree complaints; may indicate larger public space degradation
No constituent services or CB budget request data available—potential service gap
reporting_angles: Where are encampments located—parks, transit hubs, residential blocks?
What triggered the sudden spike: policy change, weather, service cuts?
How are residents and business owners responding?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 700% to 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score 4.95), suggesting either aggressive city enforcement or an influx of unlicensed vendors—possibly tied to the outdoor dining surge and active rezonings that may be attracting street commerce.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score 4.95)
Coincides with outdoor dining spike (1500% increase this week)—may be related phenomenon
Active rezonings may be changing commercial activity patterns in district
reporting_angles: Is the city stepping up vendor enforcement or are there more unlicensed vendors?
Are street food vendors operating in conflict with new outdoor dining establishments?
